failures.criterion: CI green at the head (the repository's required `ci-ok`), which the merge gate rests on
failures.evidence: The `envoy-infra-go` lane is red on this change, deterministically, and the cause is this change's own grant. Run 40882940195 at d2c92176 ended `failure`: `--- FAIL: TestDispatchPermissionsOnRealServers/hub/without_the_delivery_consumer_create_Dispatch_leaves_only_that_intake_unbound` and the same subtest under `2.10`, both at `packages/envoy/infra/core/dispatch_permissions_live_test.go:267`, message `consumer delivery-events was created despite its missing permission, or its read failed`; `ci-ok` is red with it (https://github.com/sjawhar/legion/actions/runs/40882940195/job/123486011692). The subtest (lines 97-114) removes the one subject `$JS.API.CONSUMER.CREATE.ENVOY_NOTIFICATIONS.delivery-events.>` from `core.DispatchPermissions` and requires that Dispatch can then not create its `delivery-events` durable. This change makes that impossible: `DispatchPermissions` is `ListenerPermissions` plus its own durables (`permissions.go:138-155`), and `ListenerPermissions` now carries `$JS.API.CONSUMER.CREATE.ENVOY_NOTIFICATIONS.*` and `$JS.API.CONSUMER.CREATE.ENVOY_NOTIFICATIONS.*.>`, which subsume the removed subject. I proved that without a NATS container, by printing the grant this head builds: `cd packages/envoy/infra && go run <probe>` over `core.DispatchPermissions("m1")` lists both wildcards beside the named `delivery-events` entry. The red test needs no writing: it is already in the repository and it is the one the merge gate reads. Nothing in round 2 touched `infra/core`, so it is still red at this head. Two remedies, and the choice is the architect's rather than mine, because it is the breadth of a grant: give the session-consumer entries to the listener user alone, so Dispatch and the host users keep the per-durable scope they had and the test passes unchanged; or accept that Dispatch and every host user may now create, read, delete and consume any consumer of `ENVOY_NOTIFICATIONS`, including another listener's durable and any session's `s-<id>`, and rewrite the subtest to assert what the widened grant means, with the isolation it guarded named as gone in `packages/envoy/infra/README.md` and `docs/nats-hub.md`. The plan's gap analysis accepted a wider grant on the trusted users, so the second is defensible, but the test is evidence that a property changed and it must not be left red.

observations: Not attributed to this change, and CI cannot see it: `bun test packages/claude-envoy packages/pi-envoy` in one invocation fails two pi-envoy tests ('the drift heal names the live id for the dispatch command and reads that id's ledger' and 'AskGate > the session's processes are told DISPATCH_STATE_DIR…'), where the second reads `Received: "/legion/scratch/state/tester/dispatch"`, the pod's ambient value, instead of the test's own temporary one. Each package alone is green, and `bun test packages/envoy-client packages/pi-envoy` is green, so it is an environment leak between the claude-envoy and pi-envoy suites when they share one bun process. It is not one of the two claude-envoy test files round 2 changed, nor `dist-fresh.test.ts`: adding either to a pi-envoy run leaves it green. CI runs each package in its own job, so no lane sees it; the repository's documented root `bun test` does. I could not test it against main without a second install, so I do not claim this change introduced it.

The headline guarantee does not reach production at the merge. On the core path — every hub until its VM is replaced with the new grant, and every session still on an older plugin — the role events a session misses while it is killed or cut off are still lost, which my own core-path run shows as eight zeros. The implementer records it as a deviation and the pull request body carries it as risk (1). It is the architect's to weigh, not a defect of the code.

The grant breadth behind failure 1 is a security-relevant widening, not only a red test: with `$JS.API.CONSUMER.CREATE/INFO/DELETE/MSG.NEXT.ENVOY_NOTIFICATIONS.*` in `ListenerPermissions`, and `DispatchPermissions` and `HostPermissions` built from it, Dispatch and every host user may create, read, delete and pull any consumer of the stream, another listener's durable and any session's `s-<id>` among them. `packages/envoy/infra/core/permissions.go:42-57` says so and the plan accepted it for the trusted users; the red test is where that acceptance meets a check that was written to forbid it.
